about.tagline: Download posts, attachments and whole creators from Pawchive. The desktop sibling of the browser extension.
about.featureBrowse: Browse posts, creators and searches with file picking and filters
about.featureCreators: Whole creators, scanned politely while downloads already run
about.featureResume: Resumable downloads that survive pauses, network drops and restarts
about.featureZip: ZIP archives with no size limit, split into parts if you like
about.featureRelay: Full files for preview-only posts through temporary links
about.featureVerify: Every file checked against its SHA-256 checksum
about.featureTemplates: Folder and file name templates with a live preview

about.featureWatch: Watchlist that finds new posts and can download them

about.step1: Paste a post or creator link into Browse, or drop links onto the window.
about.step2: Pick the files or posts you want and filter by type or date.
about.step3: Choose separate files, a ZIP archive or thumbnails, then press Download.
about.step4: Follow progress in Downloads or the tray. Close the window and it keeps going.

help.description: How everything works, in short. Search for a word to find the right part.
help.start.title: Your first download
help.start.body:
Copy a link from pawchive.pw and paste it into the bar at the top of Browse, or press Ctrl+L and paste. A post opens with its files, a creator with their posts.
Pick what you want, check the options in the bar at the bottom and press Download. The download appears in Downloads, where you can follow, pause or cancel it.
help.post.title: Downloading a post
help.post.body:
A post shows every file with a thumbnail. Click files to select them, Shift+Click to select a range, and use the type chips to filter. Files you already have are marked Saved.
The Text tab shows the post's description. Save post text stores it next to the files as content.txt.
help.creator.title: Downloading a creator
help.creator.body:
A creator page loads their posts 50 at a time. Search their posts on the site, limit them by date, or filter loaded posts by title and file type.
With nothing selected, Download all scans the whole creator in the background and starts downloading while it is still scanning. Select posts to download only those.
help.batch.title: Batch queue and URL import
help.batch.body: Batch (Ctrl+Shift+B) takes any number of links: paste them, import a text file, or drag them onto the window. Every creator link becomes a download of that creator; posts from the same creator are grouped into one download.
help.formats.title: Separate files, ZIP and thumbnails
help.formats.body:
Separate files saves each post into its own folder, named by the templates in Settings. ZIP writes one archive per post, with no size limit; Settings can split very large posts into parts.
Thumbnails saves only the previews and post text. It is the fallback for when Pawchive's media servers are down.
help.queue.title: The download queue
help.queue.body:
Downloads run in queue order, up to the number of simultaneous downloads set in Settings. Move a waiting download up or to the top to run it sooner.
Pause keeps partly downloaded files; Resume continues them. Failed files are retried automatically with growing pauses, and you can retry them by hand from the item list.
help.resume.title: Resuming and checksums
help.resume.body: Files are written as .part files and continue where they stopped after a pause, a dropped connection or a restart of the app. Each finished file is checked against the SHA-256 checksum in its Pawchive address, and downloaded again if it does not match.
help.preview.title: Preview-only files
help.preview.body: Pawchive keeps only a preview of some files. The full version is usually offered through a temporary link on the post's page, which the app finds and uses. Settings can save the preview instead, or skip such files.
help.watch.title: Watchlist
help.watch.body: Watch a creator to have the app look for new posts on a schedule. New posts show a badge and a notification. Turn on automatic download per creator to queue new posts as soon as they are found.
help.favorites.title: Favorites
help.favorites.body: The star on a post or creator adds it to Favorites. Add a note, download it again in one click, and export or import the list as a text file with one link per line.
help.naming.title: File and folder names
help.naming.body: Templates in Settings decide where files go inside the download folder, for example Pawchive/{creator}/{published:YYYY-MM-DD} {title}. Every value is cleaned so it is valid on Windows, macOS and Linux and cannot leave the download folder.
help.network.title: Proxy and Tor
help.network.body: Settings, Network can send every request through a proxy (http, https or socks5) or through Tor running on this computer. A speed limit keeps downloads from taking all your bandwidth.
help.tray.title: Tray and background
help.tray.body: Closing the window keeps the app in the tray, where downloads and watchlist checks continue. The tray menu pauses or resumes everything, checks the watchlist and quits. Progress also shows on the taskbar button.
help.polite.title: Why downloads are paced
help.polite.body: Pawchive asks clients for at most five downloads at once and one new request per second. The app follows that, and when the site answers that it is busy, every request waits for as long as it asks. This keeps the site fast for everyone.
help.trouble.title: When something goes wrong
help.trouble.body:
If files fail with HTTP 503 or time out, the media servers are busy: the app retries by itself, or try again later. If nothing loads, check your connection and proxy settings.
The Logs page explains what happened; copy it into a report on GitHub if you need help.
help.privacy.title: Privacy
help.privacy.body: There are no accounts, analytics or tracking. Everything the app remembers stays in its folder on this computer, and you can clear it at any time.
